No open PR touches either path.

## The gate this card sat behind is open — that is why it is dispatchable now

Triage's 2026-08-17 promotion: the standing HOLD deferred to **#3398**'s architecture ruling on the builtin branch's fate ("if #3398 goes direction C this card auto-dissolves"). #3398 closed 2026-08-10 via PR #4193 with **direction A** — one fullscreen long-text editor, hoisted to `packages/components`. **The builtin branch survives**, so this parity gap is permanent until fixed, and PR #4193 is the precedent for the fix shape: hoist the counter piece the same way the editor was hoisted, then wire the builtin `case 'textarea'` to it.

Read PR #4193 first. Mirroring an established hoist beats inventing a second one.

## ⛔ Zone 2 — the card's own unverified half is a PRECONDITION, not a footnote

The filer explicitly did **not** verify this and said so:

> 内建分支把 `stripRendererOnlyProps(fieldProps)` 展开到元素上,`maxLength` 是 textarea 的合法 DOM 属性,**有可能**顺着 `rest` 落到元素上拿到硬截断。我没有追 `ObjectForm` → FormField → `fieldProps` 这一段映射。

**Establish that first.** If `maxLength` does reach the element, the gap is only the counter and the accessible limit. If it does not, the gap also includes hard truncation and the fix widens to that mapping — **say so in the PR** rather than fixing only the visible half. Triage repeated this as premise-first for a reason.

Line references are stale by design across five re-checks (`:2097` → `:1480` → `:1490` → `:2696`) — take them from the tree, never from the card.

## Zone 3 — what the parity actually has to cover

The registered path (`packages/fields/src/widgets/TextAreaField.tsx`) ships four things; the builtin path ships none of them:
1. native `maxLength` hard truncation;
2. a visible `{n}/{max}` count (`aria-hidden`);
3. a description node wired via `aria-describedby` so the limit is announced on focus;
4. a threshold-gated, debounced `aria-live="polite"` near-limit notice.

**Items 3 and 4 are the ones that matter most and are easiest to skip.** A screen-reader user on the builtin path currently gets *no* limit information at all — the limit only appears as a validation error after submission. Delivering the visible counter and calling it parity would fix the sighted half and leave the accessibility half exactly as broken. Do not do that.

This card is the fourth or fifth member of a family the repo has ruled on repeatedly (#3272, #3400/PR #3401, #3402, #3404), and the standing line is: **one form-level declaration must produce one behaviour on both paths.**

## Fork clause

If you find the builtin branch is a **deliberately lean fallback** with a recorded rationale — the filer flagged this as plausible — stop and report `needs_decision` rather than forcing parity. But note the bar: a *recorded* rationale, not an inference from the code being thin. If none exists, the family ruling above applies and you proceed. Either way, if the outcome is that the gap stays, write the trade-off into `form.tsx` so the next person who scans this does not re-derive it — the filer asked for that explicitly.

## Gates

Derive from your diff — expect `Lint`, `Type Check`, the four test shards, changeset gates, `Control Byte Scan`. A clue, not a spec. Run the **consumer radius** if you touch `packages/fields` exports. Changeset required.

## Deliver

Draft PR against `main`, first line `Fixes #3439`. Push the branch early. Return the JSON report AND post it as an issue comment whose first line is `<!-- os-dev-report -->`.

**ACCEPT** — PR #5200 (`repo:objectui` seat PM, session `session_01AMHbqfPiETJHA95r6WzZWS`, reviewer of record).

## The precondition was the whole card, and the answer was a split nobody had

The filer flagged, honestly, that they had not traced whether `maxLength` reaches the built-in branch's element. Measured on `origin/main` @ `feb6b161d`, the answer is worse than either branch of their guess:

- the built-in branch **never reads the cap at all** — it only spreads leftover field props onto the element;
- so camelCase `maxLength` reached the DOM **by coincidence**, because it happens to name a real attribute, and gave truncation;
- while the legacy `max_length` spelling landed as a **stray inert `max_length="100"` attribute with `maxlength: null`** — i.e. **no cap whatsoever** for one of the two authored spellings.

So the gap was not "counter + accessible limit"; it was counter + accessible limit **+ hard truncation for half the authoring surface**. Anyone who took the card at face value would have shipped the visible half and left a documented `max_length` silently unenforced. That is exactly why the precondition was non-negotiable, and it earned its keep.

## The hoist — you improved on my instruction rather than following it

I said: *prefer keeping `@object-ui/fields` re-exporting `CharacterCount` so no consumer breaks.* You checked and declined, correctly:

> `CharacterCount` was never in the `@object-ui/fields` barrel and its only consumer was `TextAreaField` inside that package, so nothing can break and **NO re-export was added** — adding one would mint a public export of `@object-ui/fields` that never existed

My instruction was written to preserve a public surface. There was no public surface to preserve, and following it literally would have **created** one. Verified against the tree: the fields barrel carries no `CharacterCount` export. The move mirrors PR #4193's measured direction (fields → components, one-way) rather than inventing a second hoist pattern.

You also avoided a trap I did not warn you about: making the built-in control a component (`BuiltinTextarea`) because `FormControl` is a Radix **Slot**, and a bare wrapper `div` would have stolen `id` / `aria-describedby` / `aria-invalid` — objectui#3976's exact mechanism. Wrapping was the obvious move and it would have silently broken the accessibility this card exists to deliver.

## Ablation leg A is the one that proves the suite, not just the fix

> delete the description node's id → **7 failed / 15 passed**, and the failures are exactly the a11y assertions while **every visible-digits assertion stayed GREEN**

That asymmetry is the whole point. I told you the failure mode I feared was "ship the sighted half and call it parity". Leg A demonstrates the suite can *tell those two apart* — a green counter with a broken accessible limit fails. Most reverse verifications prove the fix works; this one proves the tests would notice the specific way this card could be under-delivered.

Leg B (drop the legacy `max_length` read → exactly 2 red, both legacy-spelling cases, with "never leaks `max_length` onto the DOM" staying green as predicted, since the strip is independent of resolution) and leg C (cross-package type change, which genuinely required a `dist` rebuild because tsc resolves through package exports while vitest aliases to src — stated with the reason, not assumed) round it out properly.

## Fork clause, properly discharged

You looked for a recorded lean-fallback rationale, found none repo-wide, and noted the record rules the other way — the 2026-08-10 ruling on #3398 plus #3272 / #3393 / #3400 / #3402 / #4824 all pulling this same branch toward parity. That is the bar I set (a *recorded* rationale, not an inference from thin code), and you cleared it before proceeding rather than after.

All four affordances now render on **both** built-in surfaces (inline and fullscreen dialog), with the `aria-live` near-limit notice inline-only, matching #3417's ruling rather than over-delivering.

## Verified against the tree

9 files, confined to `packages/components` + `packages/fields` + changeset. **OUT list clean** — nothing in `packages/app-shell`, `plugin-grid` or `plugin-kanban`, so all three sibling claims this round were respected.

**One thing I fixed rather than asked you to:** the branch did not contain current `main` (`57e668f13` landed while you were working). I have synced it via a branch update rather than enqueuing stale — in this repo that matters more than usual, because objectui#4986 records that the merge queue has never produced a `merge_group` build, so nothing would have re-validated a stale branch against current `main` on the way in.

Your out-of-scope card **#5201** (the built-in `input` branch has the identical split) records that the required search-before-filing **could not be performed** — GitHub returned rate-limit errors on three attempts — and you wrote that failure into the issue body so triage can dedupe.
